publications.title: Modal identification of structures by a novel approach based on FDD-wavelet method
publications.structure_type: generic (numerical MDOF systems with regular and irregular mass/stiffness)
methods: modified Morlet wavelet with two free parameters
publications.key_findings: Hybrid FDD-Wavelet OMA: FDD gives frequencies and mode shapes, CWT of the cyclically averaged correlation functions gives damping. Works for weak (ambient) and strong (earthquake) records, short or long. Optimal Morlet parameters come from minimizing entropy. Results beat the classic methods and match exact numerical solutions.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Validation in this paper is on numerical models. Field application was left to later work (Karun IV, Pacoima).
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad as first author. Co-author Damadipour is a known collaborator. Already Consensus-verified and found again in query 1.

publications.title: Extended FDD-WT method based on correcting the errors due to non-synchronous sensing of sensors
publications.structure_type: arch dam (Pacoima Dam, 13 Jan 2001 earthquake) + 3DOF numerical
publications.key_findings: Extends FDD-WT to correct time delays between sensors that are not synchronized. PHAT-beta was chosen as the TDE method for noisy records. The corrected modal parameters of Pacoima Dam agree with the 4-Spectral method and with the literature.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Aims to extend the method to large structures where sensors are not synchronized. Validation used one theoretical example and one dam earthquake.
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad as first author. Web search confirms the authors are Tarinejad and Damadipour. Already Consensus-verified and found again in query 4. The DOI is left empty because only the ScienceDirect PII was found.

publications.title: Modal identification of Karun IV arch dam based on ambient vibration tests and seismic responses
publications.structure_type: arch dam (Karun IV, highest concrete arch dam in Iran)
publications.key_findings: OMA of Karun IV from ambient tests (19 Mar 2014) and an earthquake (3 Mar 2015, epicentre about 133 km away). Nine natural frequencies were identified from the ambient records and four from the seismic ones. The stabilization diagram and ACS separated spurious modes from true ones.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Fewer modes are identifiable from the distant, weak seismic response than from the ambient tests.
publications.belongs_reason: Tarinejad is first author. Co-authors Ahmadi (Tarbiat Modares PhD link) and Aalami (Tabriz) fit his profile. Already Consensus-verified and found again in query 10.

publications.title: Operational modal analysis of structures using a new time-frequency domain approach
publications.venue: 6th International Operational Modal Analysis Conference (IOMAC'15), Gijon, Spain
publications.key_findings: Conference version of the FDD-CWT/CACF time-frequency OMA approach.
publications.belongs_reason: Already Consensus-verified (URL from the task, not found again in this sweep). Web search confirms Tarinejad and Damadipour (University of Tabriz) at IOMAC'15.

publications.title: Full-scale experimental modal analysis of an arch dam: The first experience in Iran
publications.structure_type: arch dam (Shahid Rajaee concrete arch dam, northern Iran)
methods: forced vibration test with crest-mounted exciters (in-phase / out-of-phase)
on-off and frequency-sweep tests (0.1 Hz steps)
FE model calibrated with earlier ambient tests
publications.key_findings: First full-scale forced-vibration modal test of an arch dam in Iran. Nine middle modes and their damping ratios were estimated up to 14 Hz. Eight modes agree well with the calibrated FE model of the dam-reservoir-foundation system.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: The exciters had limited maximum force and there were too few sensors, so two sensor arrangements were needed. The lowest modes were not captured; the later B-SSI paper (2018) reanalysed the data and found them.
publications.belongs_reason: Tarinejad is first author, with Ahmadi (Tarbiat Modares, PhD supervisor) and Harichandran (known collaborator). This matches the leads exactly.

publications.title: Modal identification of arch dams using balanced stochastic subspace identification
publications.structure_type: arch dam (Shahid Rajaee forced-vibration data; Pacoima Dam 2001 San Fernando earthquake records)
publications.key_findings: New OMA method that identifies directly in the prediction space using orthonormal vectors of the data space. Reanalysing the Shahid Rajaee forced-vibration tests gave more accurate frequencies and the first three modes, which the earlier analysis missed. On Pacoima, frequencies and damping were accurate and computation time fell by up to 50%.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Motivated by uncertainty from unknown forces, ambient noise and measurement error. Follow-up papers study uncertainty and Hankel-dimension sensitivity (Karun IV, 2022/23).
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus and the SAGE listing show Reza Tarinejad as first author with Mehran Pourgholi. Arch-dam OMA topic, consistent with the Shahid Rajaee test series.

publications.title: Automated modal analysis of an arch dam using a hybrid SSI framework based on error analysis and fuzzy clustering
methods: condition number of the observability matrix
publications.key_findings: Automated SSI-COV for the recent condition of Pacoima Dam. Identified frequencies match the FEM and earlier studies with an average difference under 8%. Damping ratios are close to earlier studies, especially the 2002 forced vibration test, despite closely spaced modes.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Existing OMA assumes white-noise, stationary inputs, which adds uncertainty. This framework tries to reduce that uncertainty but still relies on those assumptions.
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus lists 'Reza Tarinejad et al.' as authors. Web search gives the authors as Tarinejad, Hafezi and Pourgholi (published Sept 2025). Same Pacoima/SSI line as his B-SSI work. DOI not found.

publications.title: Structural system identification based on combining weighted transmissibility and wavelet transform
publications.venue: Structural Control and Health Monitoring, 29(2), e2868 (online 2021)
publications.structure_type: arch dam (Karun 3) + numerical model under El Centro
methods: CWT skeletons / single-frequency signals of correlation functions
publications.key_findings: Integrated time-frequency method with both parametric and non-parametric features for seismic responses. Weighted transmissibility gives frequencies and mode shapes, and wavelet ridges/skeletons give damping. Validated on a numerical El Centro model and applied to Karun 3 arch dam records from several earthquakes.
publications.belongs_reason: Web search confirms Reza Tarinejad (Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Tabriz) is a co-author, with frequent co-author Damadipour as first author. publications.title: Seismic modal identification using a new approach based on weighted transmissibility
methods: single-reference weighted transmissibility combined in matrix form
publications.key_findings: Standard transmissibility OMA does poorly on short seismic records because of spectral leakage and dispersion. Weighted transmissibility over one or more loading conditions, followed by SVD, correctly identifies frequencies and mode shapes.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Validated only on a theoretical 5DOF example. Field application came in the STC 2022 paper (Karun 3).
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus shows 'M. Damadipour et al.'. Web search lists it among Tarinejad and Damadipour's joint papers and gives the authors as Damadipour, Tarinejad and Aminfar, but this was inferred from related citations because the Wiley page was blocked.

publications.title: Weighted Transmissibility-Based Operational Modal Analysis for Identification of Structures Using Seismic Responses
publications.venue: Iranian Journal of Science and Technology, Transactions of Civil Engineering
methods: PIS(omega) function from singular values of weighted transmissibility matrices
publications.key_findings: Proposes weighted-transmissibility OMA for short seismic records with high spectral leakage, using the PIS(omega) indicator. Demonstrated on 2-, 3-, 5- and 10-DOF examples.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Theoretical examples only.
publications.belongs_reason: Web search gives the authors as Damadipour, Tarinejad and Aminfar. Consensus shows 'M. Damadipour et al.' Consensus gives the year as 2020 (online first); the print issue may be 2021.

publications.title: System identification of Karun IV Dam using balanced stochastic subspace algorithm considering the uncertainty of results
methods: coefficient-of-variation sensitivity analysis of Hankel matrix dimensions
publications.key_findings: Studies how Hankel-matrix user parameters (columns, block rows) affect the uncertainty of Karun IV modal estimates. Condition number, DBSCAN and MCF remove noise and computational modes. The first mode was extracted within 10% of the numerical model.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Uncertainty from output-only identification is still a challenge, and results depend on user-defined Hankel parameters.
publications.belongs_reason: Web search gives the authors as Pourgholi, Tarinejad, Khabir and Mohammadzadeh Gilarlue (JVC 2023, 29(23-24)). It continues Tarinejad's B-SSI and Karun IV work.

publications.title: Damage detection based on system identification of concrete dams using an extended finite element-wavelet transform coupled procedure
publications.structure_type: concrete arch dam (Karun III used as case per ResearchGate figure)
publications.key_findings: Couples XFEM-COH cracking simulation with CWT-based identification to find when seismic cracking starts and where the damage is, without placing an initial crack. Comparing intact and damaged modal parameters shows the history of physical changes and small system changes. The final crack profile under strong motion is also obtained.

publications.belongs_reason: The SAGE listing names the authors as Pirboudaghi, Reza Tarinejad and Mohammad Taghi Alami. M.T. Alami/Aalami of Tabriz also co-authored the Karun IV paper.

publications.structure_type: gravity dam (Koyna Dam, three excitation records)
publications.key_findings: Reduces spectral leakage near poles and separates closely spaced modes better in short earthquake records. publications.title: Response of an arch dam to non-uniform excitation generated by a seismic wave scattering model
methods: generation of non-uniform ground motion from a single site record
comparison with recorded responses (2008 Chino Hills earthquake, Pacoima Dam)
publications.key_findings: Computed displacements under the generated non-uniform excitation agree well with recorded dam responses. Uniform excitation underestimates displacements. Non-uniform input strongly increases stresses near the foundation and changes the stress pattern: maximum stresses move from the crown cantilever near the crest (uniform input) to the sides and the foundation (non-uniform input).
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Implied: a linear substructure analysis (EACD-3D-2008) validated against a single earthquake (Chino Hills 2008) at a single dam.
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad as first author. A web search confirms the author list Tarinejad, Fatehi and Harichandran, which matches the known collaborator R.S. Harichandran. The topic (arch dam, wave scattering) is his core line. The DOI comes from a web-search summary of the ScienceDirect page; the page itself could not be fetched.

publications.title: Full-scale experimental modal analysis of an arch dam: The first experience in Iran
methods: forced vibration field tests (two exciter types, in-phase/out-of-phase)
calibrated finite-element model with dam-reservoir-foundation interaction
publications.key_findings: The tests identified nine middle modes of the coupled system of the Shahid Rajaee arch dam (northern Iran), with their damping ratios, up to 14 Hz. For eight middle modes the results agree well with a finite-element model calibrated from earlier ambient tests.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Exciters had limited maximum force. There were too few sensors, so two sensor arrangements were needed. Frequencies were limited to 14 Hz.
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad. A web search (University of New Haven Digital Commons) confirms the authors Tarinejad, M.T. Ahmadi and Harichandran, who are his PhD supervisor and a known collaborator.

publications.title: Analysis of Topographic Amplification Effects on Canyon Sites Using 3D Boundary Element Method
publications.venue: Journal of Seismology and Earthquake Engineering (JSEE), 9(1), 63-72
methods: parametric study of model, wave and material parameters
publications.key_findings: Canyon length matters more than free-field length for accuracy, and the paper proposes modelling rules for 3D BEM wave scattering. The effect of canyon shape and depth on amplification depends on frequency. Deep (semi-circular) canyons amplify more than shallow (semi-elliptical) ones.
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad. A web search gives the authors Tarinejad, Ahmadi and Khaji, which fits his Tarbiat Modares PhD period ('Seismic Loading for Canyon Site Structures').

publications.title: Seismic Wave Scattering Analysis using a 3D Boundary Element Method on Topographic Irregularities
methods: parametric study (free-field/canyon length, frequency, incidence direction, damping, Poisson ratio)
publications.key_findings: Free-field length matters little compared with canyon length. Damping, incidence angle and frequency strongly affect scattering, and damped systems show larger displacements on the canyon side facing the incoming wave. Wave parameters change the displacement pattern, while material properties do not.
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad et al. The content repeats his 2007 JSEE 3D-BEM canyon work. The venue (likely a conference paper) and co-authors could not be verified.

publications.title: A new boundary element solution to evaluate the geometric effects of the canyon site on the displacement response spectrum
methods: parametric study of canyon widening ratio and SH-wave parameters
publications.key_findings: Canyon shape strongly affects displacement amplification, especially at the edges. Amplification patterns become complex for dimensionless frequency above 1. The paper gives a new expression for the limiting wavelength beyond which canyon widening no longer matters, validated against published results.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Implied: limited to semi-circular canyons and shear waves in an elastic half-space.
publications.belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad as first author. A web search confirms Tarinejad, Isari and Taghavi Ghalesari (his University of Tabriz group).

publications.title: A new approach to generating non-uniform support excitation at topographic sites
methods: validation with Pacoima Dam records (two earthquakes)
publications.key_findings: The paper derives regression relations for the time delay and the spectral coherence function of V-shaped canyons, which flat-site coherence models cannot represent. They agree with Pacoima Dam records and are used to simulate non-uniform support accelerations.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Existing coherence models come from flat-surface data and do not suit topographic sites, which is the gap this paper addresses. The relations are specific to V-shaped canyons.
publications.belongs_reason: A web search gives the full author list, which includes Reza Tarinejad (University of Tabriz) and his usual co-authors Isari, Taghavi Ghalesari and Sohrabi-Bidar.

publications.title: A procedure to predict the precise seismic response of arch dams in time domain using boundary element formulation
publications.venue: Journal of Rock Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering, 11(4), 790-803
methods: time-domain BEM with time-convoluted traction kernels (BEMSA)
3D model of the Pacoima Dam canyon
SH, SV and P incident waves
publications.key_findings: Dam-site response depends on the incident wave's predominant frequency, the topography, the relative distance of observation points and the wave type. Incident SV waves gave the largest amplification, especially on the left side of the dam.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Uses a linearly elastic constitutive model for the medium.
publications.belongs_reason: A web search gives the authors TaghaviGhalesari, Isari, Tarinejad and Sohrabi-Bidar, all known co-authors. The topic is the same Pacoima time-domain BEM line.

code for generating spatially varying ground motion
publications.key_findings: The paper proposes a function for the time delay at topographic sites, depending on height above the canyon base, wave velocity and predominant frequency. It estimates delays accurately enough to generate non-uniform ground motion.

publications.belongs_reason: Consensus lists R. Tarinejad as first author. A web search confirms Tarinejad, Isari and Sohrabi-Bidar.

publications.title: Investigation of seismic response of topography under recorded excitation using boundary element method
methods: recorded input from valley bottom (2001 Pacoima earthquake)
publications.key_findings: Amplification grows from the bottom to the top of the valley at most frequencies. The displacement amplification ratio reaches about 3 along the valley, so non-uniform motion should be considered for large structures.
publications.belongs_reason: A web search confirms the authors Isari, Tarinejad and Alavi (SN Applied Sciences, Nov 2020). The topic is consistent with the Tabriz BEM group.

methods: SV-wave parametric analysis over predominant frequency and shape ratio

publications.title: Modal Identification of a Soil-subway System with Emphasis on Scattering of Seismic Waves Induced by Uniform and Non-uniform Support Excitations
publications.venue: Journal of Earthquake Engineering, 26(12) (issue dated 2022; online 2021)
publications.key_findings: The extended FRFM-SVD method identifies the seismic behaviour of the underground structure with reasonable accuracy. Maximum amplification near the subway is about 1.75 under non-uniform excitation, roughly 20% more than under uniform excitation.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Recommends combining the presence of underground structures with non-uniform excitation to estimate surface accelerations accurately.
publications.belongs_reason: A web search (T&F page) gives the authors Isari, Razavi and Tarinejad, all University of Tabriz. The methods (FRFM-SVD, wavelet) are Tarinejad's system-identification line.

publications.title: Numerical study on the influence of near-fault and far-fault earthquakes on a subway station with emphasis to scattering on the wave propagation
methods: parametric study of embedment and station dimensions
publications.key_findings: A subway station causes frequency-dependent amplification or de-amplification at the surface. Surface acceleration rose about 1.3 times under far-fault earthquakes, and relative displacement rose about 1.6 times.
publications.belongs_reason: A web search gives the authors Isari, Hadidi, Razavi and Tarinejad. This resolves the 'subway-station near-/far-fault scattering' lead as Tarinejad's paper.

publications.title: Evaluation the effects of Wave Scattering Resonance from Complex Topographies Using Boundary Element Method
methods: SH waves at varying incidence angles and dimensionless frequencies
publications.key_findings: The parts of a canyon next to a hill amplify most, especially when the two are close. Incidence angle strongly controls the displacement pattern, and even vertical incidence gives asymmetric patterns because of scattering.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Notes that interaction between adjacent topographic irregularities has received little attention.
publications.belongs_reason: A web search gives the authors Isari, Tarinejad, Sobhkhiz Foumani and Taghavi Ghalesari, all known Tabriz co-authors.

result.disambiguation_notes:
I could only partly verify things. ORCID, Crossref and OpenAlex were blocked by the egress proxy (403), and Google Scholar, ResearchGate, ScienceDirect, Springer, MDPI and most Iranian journal sites were blocked for WebFetch. Author lists therefore come from the Consensus author field plus WebSearch result summaries, not from publisher pages.

The Consensus monthly quota (30) ran out after 12 successful queries. The 13th (Pirboudaghi spectral element) failed, so later items have no Consensus URL and are marked evidence_source=websearch.

Every accepted item has Tarinejad in the author list and fits the University of Tabriz group. Recurring co-authors: Mohsen Isari, Abbasali Taghavi Ghalesari, Abdollah Sohrabi-Bidar (University of Tehran, geology), Seyyed Kazem Razavi, Ramtin Sobhkhiz Foumani, Sajjad Pirboudaghi, Farhoud Kalateh. Earlier co-authors from his Tarbiat Modares PhD period: M.T. Ahmadi and N. Khaji. US collaborators: R.S. Harichandran and R. Fatehi. A web result names his TMU PhD dissertation as 'Seismic Loading for Canyon Site Structures', which matches the 2007-2009 canyon BEM papers.

Uncertain fields:
- The 2013 SDEE DOI (10.1016/j.soildyn.2013.04.011) comes from a search summary, not the publisher page.
- The Legendre SEM paper is cited as 2014 in places, but IJCE 13(2) is 2015.
- The BESE Pacoima topography paper is vol. 6 (Iranian year 1398), approximately 2019.
- The venue of the 2021 Persian stochastic Karun-4 paper and the 2009 3D-BEM scattering paper is unknown.

Web leads:
- Subway-station near-/far-fault scattering paper: confirmed as Tarinejad's (Isari, Hadidi, Razavi, Tarinejad, NMCE 2023).
- Seepage in Short Embankments (Applied Sciences 2020): confirmed. Tarinejad is the 5th of 7 authors (Tang et al.).
- Damadipour 2022 STC and Vaseti 2026 Engineering Reports: not checked in this sweep. They belong to other clusters.

Possible gaps for other agents:
- Pouya et al. 2021 (Karun III non-uniform motions) may need a co-author check.
- Tarinejad-Pourgholi 2018 and Pirboudaghi-Tarinejad-Alami 2018 (both J. Vibration and Control) were found incidentally and belong to the SHM cluster.

publications.title: Optimized Mesh Zoning for Dam Bottom Outlet CFD Simulations Using Richardson Extrapolation and Grid Convergence Analysis
publications.key_findings: Systematic mesh-zoning based on Richardson extrapolation and GCI picks locally optimal resolutions. The zoned grid cuts total cell count by about 35-40% versus uniform refinement while keeping deviations below about 2-3% in discharge coefficient, wall pressure distribution and key flow-field parameters.
publications.belongs_reason: Wiley listing and search snippet give the author list Vaseti, Akhtari, Reza Tarinejad. Hydraulic-structures topic matches his listed expertise. Confirms the web lead.

publications.title: A Novel Complex Frequency-Domain Approach Using Power Spectral Density Transmissibility to Extract Dynamic Characteristics
publications.key_findings: PSDT-CF uses forward and backward frequency shifts via the z-transform to build modified transmissibility functions. This suppresses spectral leakage near poles and separates closely spaced modes. Validated on Koyna Dam under three excitation records, with natural-frequency errors below 2.5% in all identified modes, beating conventional techniques.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Motivated by the large pole-identification errors of conventional methods with closely spaced modes, and by the spectral dispersion that non-periodic components in short earthquake records cause in higher modes.
publications.belongs_reason: Two separate search summaries attribute it to Tarinejad and Amanzad (University of Tabriz), published July 2026. Continues the Tarinejad-Amanzad transmissibility line. The author list was not read directly from the Springer page, which was blocked.

publications.title: Identification of operational modal parameters using multi-reference weighted Hermitian transmissibility functions
publications.venue: Journal of Sound and Vibration, vol. 615 (24 Oct 2025)
publications.key_findings: P-WHTOMA weights structural responses and defines transmissibility functions with Hermitian polynomials. This makes the normal vectors orthogonal, reduces spectral dispersion around structural poles, cuts spurious poles under several simultaneous inputs, and lowers the effect of non-periodic harmonic components.
publications.stated_limitations_or_future_work: Motivated by the inaccuracy of standard TOMA during earthquakes, where signals disperse around the poles.
publications.belongs_reason: Search summaries name Tarinejad R and Amanzad F of the Faculty of Civil Engineering, University of Tabriz. The ScienceDirect PII 0022460X is the Journal of Sound and Vibration ISSN. One search summary wrongly called the venue JVET; the PII supports JSV. DOI not seen, so left blank.

publications.title: Soft Computing and Predicting Labyrinth Gates Discharge Coefficient
methods: Support Vector Machine (RBF, polynomial, linear, sigmoid kernels)
publications.key_findings: Uses 345 experimental points (70% train, 30% test). The RBF-kernel SVM predicted Cd best. Adding a sill to a labyrinth sliding gate raised Cd by 9.9%, 11.8%, 13.4% and 20.8% for sill widths of 5, 15, 20 and 30.5 cm compared with a standard sliding gate.
publications.belongs_reason: ResearchGate listing names Abbaszadeh and Reza Tarinejad. Machine learning for hydraulic gates fits his hydraulic-structures and physical-modelling profile. One summary also mentioned a February 2026 Water Practice & Technology paper by the same pair, which a follow-up search could not confirm.

publications.title: Investigating Concrete Arch Dam Behavior Under underwater explosion (Case Study: Karun4 Dam)
publications.key_findings: The dam failed under 1300, 2000 and 2000 kg TNT detonated at 225, 115 and 5 m respectively. Reservoir water level had a negligible effect on the failure blast load.
publications.belongs_reason: Journal page lists Reza Tarinejad, Professor at the University of Tabriz, as first author. Karun-4 is a dam he has studied before. Accepted 1 Dec 2023.

publications.title: Numerical study on the influence of near-fault and far-fault earthquakes on a subway station with emphasis to scattering on the wave propagation

publications.title: Optimized Mesh Zoning for Dam Bottom Outlet CFD Simulations Using Richardson Extrapolation and Grid Convergence Analysis
publications.structure_type: bottom outlet (radial service gate + vertical emergency gate)
methods: ANSYS FLUENT 2024 R2 two-dimensional CFD model
publications.key_findings: Studies a bottom outlet with a 45 m head on the gate, a 3.5 m x 2.5 m radial service gate and a 3.5 m x 2.7 m vertical emergency gate. It proposes mesh zoning: a fine mesh near the gate opening, where hydraulic gradients are strong, and a coarser mesh upstream and downstream, where flow varies less. Zone lengths of about 4.8-6.2 m depend on the parameter, reflecting different sensitivity to turbulent structures. Velocity, pressure and turbulent kinetic energy were checked with Richardson/GCI.
